verdicts.reason: The Returning Officer guide states the Returning Officer's duty is to conduct the Dáil election in the constituency and ascertain and declare the results, which matches 'Returning Officers per constituency'.

The guide names the Election Count Database System (Ecount) made available for the count, and its count chapter (sections 22-24) describes the physical sorting, counting and recounting of ballot papers, which supports 'used alongside the manual paper-ballot count'.

The quoted sentence does not itself name the operator, but the sentence immediately before it on the same page says 'the CIS Corps continued the implementation of the DF's Next Generation Working Environment (NGWE) project' for the DF Enterprise network, which supports 'Defence Forces CIS Corps'.
The same passage names the DF Enterprise network, the NGWE project and the 'on premise national Communications Information Services Network (CISN)', matching the printed names.

The source says the NSAC was established in 2019 by the Government to provide strategic analysis to the Taoiseach and Government; it does not say NSAC operates intelligence services or the Defence Forces Military Intelligence holdings named as the register. The page attributes intelligence work to Defence Forces Military Intelligence (J2), not NSAC.

The quote names Military Intelligence as a Defence Forces function delivering security outputs; nowhere does the report name a register or system, and 'holdings' is the report's own wording. The source confirms the unit exists but not a register of that name.

The Department of Social Protection annual report states MyGovID is 'the secure online identity authentication service provided by the department', i.e. operated by a state body, so 'Yes' is supported.
The report says 'over 3.2 million actively using their MyGovID account to access online services', matching the printed figure and wording.
The report names MyGovID as the department's online identity authentication service.

Both the 2024 and 2025 Tailte Éireann annual reports say Landdirect.ie gives access to '2.4 million Folios and associated spatial data', matching the printed figure; the 2025 report quote was also found verbatim.

The 2024 annual report states that under the Tailte Éireann Act 2022, Tailte Éireann is a Civil Service body, and the same report says its Registration function is responsible for the Land Registry and Registry of Deeds.

The 2024 report says particulars are entered on folios which form the National Land Register and that the Registration function has responsibility for the Land Registry and the Registry of Deeds; the 2025 report quote on the digital National Land Register was also found verbatim.

The C&AG chapter states the Department of Finance manages the Central Fund of the Exchequer, and throughout attributes the FMSS programme and system to the National Shared Services Office (NSSO), matching both parts of the printed operator.

The FMSS system name is supported, but the page contradicts '(incl. the Exchequer)': it says the Exchequer ran FMSS in parallel from April 2022 and that in September 2022 the Department of Finance 'made the decision to pause the Exchequer's transfer to FMSS'. The source does not say the Exchequer is on FMSS.

The quoted sentence only names the ECB Guideline as the legal instrument, but the same page states T2 is 'the Eurosystem's real-time gross settlement (RTGS) system' running on 'a single technical platform' of which TARGET2-Ireland is the Irish component, which supports an EU (Eurosystem) provider rather than national infrastructure.

The page states 'The Irish component system of T2, operated by the Central Bank of Ireland, is TARGET2-Ireland'; the annual report quote on the Central Bank's data centre transition was also found verbatim.
